lines.text: She hung a bronze bell over the river, and told the Duke: if this ever rings, climb.
The whole council burst out laughing.
Under the bell, a stone well. In the well, a copper float. And from the float, a chain to the hammer.
The Duke had the tallest walls in the world. And she wanted him scared of a bucket.
Weeks later, the bell rang once. But the river stayed calm.
Not even a wave rocked the Duke's boat.
The Duke called it the world's loudest doorbell, and threw it out of the city.
So she dragged it up the river, all the way to the mountains, and lived there.
Then one night, under a clear sky, the bell rang. And rang. And did not stop.
She ran all night to the city gates.
Hey, bell lady. Your bucket thirsty again?
lines.speaker: guard

lines.text: They laughed her all the way back up the hill.
By morning, the lower city was underwater.
Inside the well, a pipe ran to the river. A little water lifted the float a little. A flood lifted it all the way, yanked the pin, and the hammer never stopped swinging.
One ring meant rain, far away. And by throwing the bell out, the Duke had moved it closer to the storm.
